- Overestimate prices when sentiment is negative (especially strong negative sentiment), especially in early forecast periods.  
- Underestimate prices after strong upward spikes in sentiment or price, particularly if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon.  
- Model tends to lag in recognizing sentiment-driven reversals — adjust forecasts upward if sentiment turns positive after a dip.  
- Overshoots in the short-term (1-3 days) after a price spike, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed.  
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high in the middle of the forecast horizon when sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative over 3+ days, reduce forecast by 2–5% relative to prior period to avoid overconfidence in downward momentum.  
- If sentiment turns positive after a negative streak, model often fails to fully capitalize — increase forecast by 1–3% per day of positive sentiment buildup.
